name: Obscurite-AM
description: A tungsten-hafnium-carbon alloy with a quantum-engineered surface phonon structure that absorbs 99.97% of incident electromagnetic radiation across all wavelengths from gamma through microwave — functioning as a structural metal with near-perfect broadband absorption. Unlike surface coatings, Obscurite-AM's absorption properties are intrinsic to the bulk material and cannot be worn away or damaged without compromising the alloy itself. The absorbed energy is converted to lattice vibration and dissipated as low-grade heat, requiring thermal management in high-irradiance applications.
applications: stealth vehicle and aircraft structural components
sensor baffling and optical trap arrays
story_hooks: A structure built from Obscurite-AM panels has appeared overnight in a mid-tier industrial zone — it shows up on no sensors, reflects no light, and has no visible entry points; the city's security apparatus is deeply unsettled and looking for anyone with knowledge of who could fabricate this.

Military surplus Obscurite-AM panels are being sold piecemeal through a Tier 2 scrap dealer who has no idea what she has — buyers range from paranoid privacy advocates to people with much more dangerous intentions.
An Obscurite-AM component from a classified installation has been stolen, and the investigation is complicated by the fact that the security footage shows nothing — because the thief was wearing it.
